name: Affinity Photo 2
note: Every row of Serif's "Keyboard shortcuts" page in the Affinity Photo 2 help. The context is the page's category with the trailing word "shortcuts" removed (Editing, Vector-specific, File, Edit, Tools, Layer operations, Painting, Text, View, Pixel selection/Mask, Workspace, Adjustment and Filter, Liquify Persona, Blend mode, Misc, macOS), plus the table's own qualifier where it has one, so the same tool name can appear under Tools and under Tools (Develop Persona only). The page holds a Windows and a macOS variant of every row in the same HTML and picks one at load time; the web build's stylesheet only ever draws the macOS glyphs, so the Windows chords here are read from the Windows variant's own markup, in which Serif's Command tag is the Ctrl key. Three rows whose macOS form uses Control sit outside the per-platform markup (Edit Live Projection, Toggle Full Screen, Delete from insertion point to end of paragraph) and are treated as macOS only. Rows that document a set of keys - the arrow keys for nudging, [ and ] for brush and stroke width, Left and Right for nozzle rotation - become one action per key with the chord repeated in parentheses. Mouse and stylus gestures are left out: everything using a drag, a click, the scroll wheel, Caps Lock or a run of numeric keys, along with the Fn-key row (Emoji & Symbols) that the chord grammar cannot express and "Setting brush hardness and flow", which Serif writes as a sentence rather than a chord. Two rows are left out because Serif's own markup prints no key at all: "Erase with Pixel Tool" and "Edit curves as you draw". Where Serif writes the key as "+" (the macOS forms of Zoom In and Superscript) it is kept as Plus rather than guessed at, and "Switch to Next View" keeps the bare ` its Windows markup gives, without the Command tag its macOS form carries.
